properties.name: Moomba CCS
properties.description: Australia's first large-scale onshore CCS project, capturing CO₂ from the Moomba gas processing plant and injecting it into depleted gas reservoirs. Started injecting in late 2024.

properties.name: Santos Basin Pre-Salt CCUS
properties.location: Santos Basin, offshore Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
properties.description: Petrobras' pre-salt CCUS program captures CO₂ from offshore FPSOs and reinjects it into pre-salt reservoirs for enhanced oil recovery, the world's largest offshore CO₂-EOR operation. A record ~14.2 Mt of CO₂ was reinjected in 2024.

properties.name: Alberta Carbon Trunk Line (ACTL)
properties.description: 240 km CO₂ pipeline network linking Redwater-area emitters to enhanced oil recovery and permanent geological storage in central Alberta, operating since 2020. Its large design capacity of ~14.6 Mtpa is far above actual utilisation.

properties.name: Glacier Gas Plant CCS
properties.description: Entropy's modular post-combustion CCS at Advantage Energy's Glacier gas plant, capturing from compression engines since 2022 and expanded in 2026 with a 15 MW cogeneration unit integrated with capture. Captures ~192,000 t/yr.

properties.name: North West Redwater Sturgeon Refinery CCS
properties.operator: North West Redwater Partnership (Canadian Natural Resources / Alberta Government)
properties.description: Gasification-based bitumen refinery that produces a pure, dry CO₂ stream captured rather than vented, serving as the anchor supply for the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line. Captures up to ~1.2 Mtpa of CO₂.

properties.name: Nutrien Redwater CCS
properties.description: Captures CO₂ from ammonia and hydrogen production at Nutrien's Redwater nitrogen complex and exports it into the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line. A 2023 expansion raised capture/export capacity to over 300,000 t/yr.

properties.name: Quest CCS
properties.description: Shell-operated amine CCS capturing CO₂ from three hydrogen manufacturing units at the Scotford Upgrader since 2015, stored ~2 km underground in the Basal Cambrian Sands. It has exceeded its ~1 Mtpa target, storing over 7 million tonnes cumulatively.

properties.name: CNOOC Enping 15-1 Offshore CCUS
properties.description: China's first offshore carbon capture, utilisation and storage project, reinjecting CO₂ separated from the Enping 15-1 oilfield into a nearby saline aquifer. Operating since 2023.

properties.name: CNPC Jilin Oilfield CO2-EOR
properties.description: China's first large-scale CO₂-EOR project, separating CO₂ from the Changling gas field and injecting it into the Jilin low-permeability oilfield for enhanced oil recovery since 2018.

properties.name: Guohua Jinjie CCS
properties.description: Post-combustion carbon capture unit on a 600 MW unit of the Guohua Jinjie coal power station, capturing around 150,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year at a 90% capture rate since 2021.

properties.name: Sinopec Qilu–Shengli CCUS
properties.description: Sinopec's flagship CCUS project, capturing CO₂ from the Qilu refinery/petrochemical complex and piping it to the Shengli oilfield for enhanced oil recovery. First phase started in 2019, expanded toward ~1 Mtpa by 2021.

properties.name: Taizhou Power Plant CCS
properties.description: Carbon capture on a coal-fired unit of the Taizhou power plant, capturing about 500,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year for utilisation and storage. Operating since 2023.

properties.name: Yanchang CCUS
properties.description: Integrated CCUS project at two coal-to-chemical plants in Yulin, capturing CO₂ for enhanced oil recovery in the Ordos Basin low-permeability reservoirs.

properties.name: Carbfix Hellisheiði
properties.description: Dissolves CO₂ in water and injects it into basalt at Hellisheiði, where it mineralises into rock; operational since 2014.

properties.name: Climeworks Mammoth
properties.description: Climeworks' larger direct air capture plant in Iceland, ramping up to about 36,000 tonnes per year with CO₂ mineralised underground by Carbfix.

properties.name: Climeworks Orca
properties.description: Climeworks' first commercial direct air capture and storage plant at Hellisheiði, capturing about 4,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year using Carbfix mineralisation.

properties.name: Ravenna CCS
properties.description: Eni-Snam joint venture CCS hub in the Adriatic; Phase 1 began injecting CO₂ in 2024, with Phase 2 targeting around 4 MtCO₂/yr of industrial emitters.

properties.name: Heidelberg Materials Brevik CCS
properties.description: First commercial-scale carbon capture at a cement plant, capturing CO₂ from the Norcem Brevik kiln for shipment to Northern Lights; captured first CO₂ during its 2025 ramp-up.

properties.name: Northern Lights
properties.description: Europe's first open-access CO₂ transport and storage network; receives liquefied CO₂ at Øygarden and injects it into a North Sea saline aquifer. Phase 1 commissioned 2024/2025.

properties.name: Sleipner CO₂ Storage
properties.description: World's first dedicated offshore CO₂ storage project, separating CO₂ from Sleipner gas production and injecting it into the Utsira saline aquifer since 1996.

properties.name: Snøhvit CO₂ Storage
properties.description: Captures CO₂ from the Melkøya LNG plant and injects it into the Tubåen formation beneath the Snøhvit field; restarted in 2022 after the 2020 plant fire.

properties.name: Ras Laffan CCS
properties.description: QatarEnergy's first CCS project, capturing ~2.2 Mtpa of CO₂ from LNG trains at Ras Laffan Industrial City for geological sequestration. Operational since 2019.

properties.name: Uthmaniyah CO₂-EOR
properties.description: Saudi Aramco's first CO₂-EOR demonstration, capturing ~0.8 Mtpa of CO₂ from the Hawiyah gas plant and piping it ~85 km to the Uthmaniyah oil field for enhanced oil recovery. Operating since 2015.

properties.name: Al Reyadah CCUS
properties.description: The MENA region's first commercial-scale CCUS facility, capturing CO₂ from Emirates Steel Arkan's plant in Mussafah and piping it ~43 km for enhanced oil recovery in ADNOC onshore fields. Operating since 2016.

properties.name: Tata Chemicals Europe CCS
properties.description: The UK's first commercial industrial carbon capture plant, capturing CO₂ from a gas-fired combined heat and power plant to produce pharmaceutical and food-grade sodium bicarbonate and salt.

properties.name: ADM Decatur (Illinois Industrial CCS)
properties.description: Ethanol plant capturing fermentation CO₂ and injecting it into the deep Mt. Simon Sandstone saline formation, one of the first large US saline-storage CCS operations.

properties.name: Air Products Port Arthur SMR
properties.description: Steam methane reformer producing hydrogen for the Valero Port Arthur refinery, with CO₂ capture. Captured CO₂ is used for enhanced oil recovery in Texas.

properties.name: Arkalon CO2 Compression Facility
properties.description: Ethanol plant CO₂ compression facility sending captured CO₂ to Kansas and Oklahoma oilfields for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Bonanza BioEnergy
properties.description: Ethanol plant capturing fermentation CO₂ for enhanced oil recovery in nearby Kansas oilfields.

properties.name: Century Plant
properties.description: Natural gas processing plant in the Permian Basin capturing CO₂ from the processed gas stream. Captured CO₂ feeds Occidental's Permian Basin enhanced oil recovery operations.

properties.name: Coffeyville Gasification Plant
properties.description: Petroleum coke gasification and nitrogen fertilizer complex capturing CO₂ from ammonia production. Captured CO₂ is transported to Kansas and Oklahoma oilfields for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Denbury/ExxonMobil Gulf Coast CO2 Network
properties.description: Large operating network of CO₂ pipelines and enhanced oil recovery fields across the Gulf Coast, including the Green Pipeline. ExxonMobil is expanding it into a CO₂ 'superhighway' for new capture projects and permanent storage.

properties.name: Enid Fertilizer Plant
properties.description: Ammonia and fertilizer plant capturing CO₂ from its steam methane reforming process. Captured CO₂ is transported for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Great Plains Synfuels Plant
properties.description: Coal-to-synthetic-natural-gas plant that captures CO₂ from its gasification process. Captured CO₂ is piped roughly 200 miles to the Weyburn and Midale fields in Saskatchewan, Canada for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Lost Cabin Gas Plant
properties.description: Natural gas processing plant capturing CO₂ from the gas stream. Captured CO₂ is compressed and piped for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Shute Creek Gas Plant (LaBarge)
properties.description: One of the world's largest operating CCS projects, capturing CO₂ from the LaBarge natural gas field's raw gas. ExxonMobil is expanding capacity toward about 8 Mtpa; CO₂ is sold for enhanced oil recovery and dedicated geologic storage.

properties.name: Stratos Direct Air Capture
properties.description: First commercial-scale US direct air capture plant, designed to remove up to 500,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. Began startup in 2025 with captured CO₂ destined for dedicated saline storage (Class VI wells) and potential EOR.

properties.name: Terrell Natural Gas Processing Plant
properties.description: Natural gas processing facility that separates and captures CO₂ from the Barnett Shale gas stream. Captured CO₂ is compressed and delivered via Denbury's pipeline network for enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Gorgon CO2 Injection
properties.description: One of the world's largest CCS projects, separating CO₂ from the Gorgon LNG plant and injecting it into a deep saline formation beneath Barrow Island. It began injecting in 2019 but has stored far below its ~4 Mtpa design target — roughly 2.5 Mt in its first five years versus ~20 Mt expected.

properties.name: Boundary Dam Unit 3 CCS
properties.description: World's first commercial-scale post-combustion CCS retrofit on a coal-fired power unit (110 MW lignite), operating since 2014. It has captured CO₂ well below its ~1 Mtpa design target, with frequent outages and low availability.

properties.name: Petra Nova
properties.description: Post-combustion amine capture system on a unit of the W.A. Parish coal plant. It captured well below its ~1.4 Mtpa design target, was idled in 2020, and restarted in late 2023 at reduced rates.

properties.name: CarbonNet
properties.description: Victorian government-backed CO₂ transport and storage network concept in the Gippsland Basin, aiming to connect Latrobe Valley industrial emitters to offshore storage.

properties.name: Gippsland Basin CCS (SE Australia)
properties.description: ExxonMobil/Esso-led project to repurpose depleted Gippsland Basin gas fields for CO₂ storage, serving industrial emitters in Victoria's Latrobe Valley and Gippsland region.

properties.name: Rio de Janeiro CCS Pilot
properties.description: Petrobras' first dedicated CCS pilot in Rio de Janeiro state, tendered in September 2025 to inject ~100,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. A step toward scaling Brazil's geological storage beyond pre-salt EOR.

properties.name: Air Products Edmonton Net-Zero Hydrogen Complex
properties.description: Net-zero hydrogen production complex in northeast Edmonton supplying blue hydrogen to Imperial Oil's Strathcona refinery, with autothermal reforming and carbon capture of roughly 1 Mtpa CO₂ for transport and storage. Construction is well underway.

properties.name: Alberta Carbon Grid
properties.description: TC Energy and Pembina Pipeline's proposed open-access CO₂ transportation and storage hub across Alberta's industrial heartland. In early development.

properties.name: Dow Fort Saskatchewan Path2Zero
properties.description: Dow's world-first net-zero Scope 1 and 2 ethylene cracker and derivatives expansion, with carbon capture and storage reducing existing emissions by ~1 Mtpa and abating all new capacity emissions. FID taken November 2023, later delayed and reaffirmed with a 2029–2030 start-up timeline.

properties.name: Enhance Energy Origins CCS Hub
properties.description: Open-access carbon capture and storage hub near Clive, Alberta, set to become Canada's largest operating sequestration facility. Broke ground in 2026 with commercial operations targeted for January 2027 and built-in expansion capacity.

properties.name: Heidelberg Materials Edmonton CCUS
properties.description: Heidelberg Materials' ~1 Mtpa cement CCUS project at its Edmonton plant, sending captured CO₂ by pipeline to the Wabamun Carbon Hub. Originally slated for late 2026, it was placed on hold in 2026 amid weak carbon pricing and regulatory uncertainty.

properties.name: Lafarge Exshaw Cement CCS
properties.description: Lafarge Canada's carbon capture development at its Exshaw cement plant in the Bow Valley, at pre-FID feasibility/pilot stage. Part of broader efforts to decarbonise Alberta cement production.

properties.name: Linde Fort Saskatchewan Clean Hydrogen
properties.description: Linde's ~$2B blue hydrogen complex at Fort Saskatchewan, using autothermal reforming with carbon capture to supply clean hydrogen to Dow's Path2Zero site. FID taken; supports the net-zero ethylene complex.

properties.name: Open Access Wabamun Carbon Hub
properties.description: Enbridge's open-access CO₂ transportation and storage hub near Wabamun, serving multiple Edmonton-region emitters including Heidelberg Materials. Approved by the Alberta government; Phase 1 targets ~1 Mtpa with expansion potential.

properties.name: Pathways Alliance CCS Hub
properties.operator: Pathways Alliance (Cenovus, Suncor, Canadian Natural, Imperial, ConocoPhillips, MEG Energy)
properties.description: Proposed oil-sands CCS network connecting ~20 facilities across the Fort McMurray and Cold Lake regions to a shared storage hub. Estimated at ~$16.5B and targeting ~10–12 Mtpa, it remains pre-FID with a decision targeted for late 2027.

properties.name: Shell Atlas Carbon Storage Hub
properties.description: CO₂ storage hub developed by Shell in partnership with ATCO EnPower near Scotford, with FID taken June 2024. Phase 1 will provide permanent storage for CO₂ captured by the Polaris project, with capacity to expand for third-party emitters.

properties.name: Shell Polaris CCS
properties.description: Second CCS unit at Shell's Scotford Energy and Chemicals Park, with FID taken June 2024 to capture ~650,000 t/yr of CO₂ from refinery and upgrader operations. Expected to start up toward the end of 2028.

properties.name: Bifrost
properties.description: Ørsted-led offshore CO₂ storage project in the Danish North Sea (Harald field), planned to store around 3 MtCO₂/yr.

properties.name: Norne CO₂ Storage Hub
properties.description: Danish onshore-to-offshore CO₂ storage hub in North Jutland, led by a TotalEnergies consortium, aiming to store CO₂ from around 2030.

properties.name: Project Greensand
properties.location: Nini West field, Danish North Sea
properties.description: Pioneering cross-border CO₂ storage in Denmark's Nini West field; completed Europe's first cross-border injection pilot in 2023 with full-scale operation planned.

properties.name: Meleiha CCS
properties.description: A small CCS pilot by Eni and EGPC at the Meleiha field in Egypt's Western Desert, targeting capture and storage of ~25,000–30,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. Announced in 2022 as Egypt's first CCS project.

properties.name: Dunkerque Industrial CCS
properties.description: Planned industrial CCS in the Dunkirk area, initially targeting ArcelorMittal's steelworks emissions for offshore storage.

properties.name: Pycasso CO₂ Storage
properties.description: Teréga and TotalEnergies' planned CO₂ transport and storage hub in south-west France using the depleted Rousse gas field.

properties.name: GeZero (Geseke)
properties.description: Heidelberg Materials' planned full-chain CCS at its Geseke cement plant, capturing CO₂ for transport to North Sea storage.

properties.name: Abadi CCS
properties.location: Abadi field, Masela Block, Arafura Sea
properties.description: INPEX-led CCS integrated with the Abadi LNG development in the Masela Block, capturing CO₂ from the gas stream for reinjection into the Abadi reservoir.

properties.name: Tangguh CCUS
properties.description: Indonesia's first CCUS project, capturing CO₂ from the Tangguh LNG plant and reinjecting it into the Ubadari reservoir. Under construction with first injection targeted around 2026/2027 and long-term capacity up to ~15 Mtpa.

properties.name: Tomakomai CCS Demonstration
properties.description: Japan's offshore CCS demonstration, which met its 300,000-tonne injection target into sub-seafloor formations by 2019 before injection was suspended. Full-scale commercial expansion is under study.

properties.name: Kasawari CCS
properties.description: Petronas's first CCS project, capturing high-CO₂ gas from the Kasawari field and reinjecting it into a nearby saline aquifer offshore Sarawak. Under construction with first injection targeted around 2027.

properties.name: Lang Lebah CCS
properties.description: Planned CCS associated with the Lang Lebah high-CO₂ gas field development offshore Sarawak, part of Petronas's growing CCS portfolio.

properties.name: Aramis CCS
properties.description: Large-scale CO₂ transport and storage initiative in the Dutch North Sea, aggregating emitters from Rotterdam and beyond for injection from around 2028/2030.

properties.name: CO2next
properties.description: Liquid CO₂ import, buffer and export terminal at Rotterdam's Maasvlakte enabling flexible CO₂ shipping.

properties.name: L10 CO₂ Storage
properties.description: Planned CO₂ storage in the depleted L10 gas field in the Dutch North Sea, led by Neptune Energy (now Eni).

properties.name: Porthos
properties.operator: Port of Rotterdam Authority / Gasunie / EBN
properties.description: Rotterdam's CO₂ transport and storage project injecting captured industrial CO₂ into depleted North Sea gas fields; under construction with first injection expected in 2026.

properties.name: Hafslund Celsio Klemetsrud CCS
properties.description: Planned CO₂ capture at Oslo's Klemetsrud waste-to-energy plant, originally part of the Longship project and now pursued by Hafslund Celsio with new partners.

properties.name: Blue Horizons
properties.description: Shell Oman's planned blue hydrogen/ammonia project with integrated CO₂ capture and dedicated geological storage, using KBR's blue ammonia technology and Wood for pre-FEED. Currently in early development.

properties.name: North Field East CCS
properties.description: A CCS project serving QatarEnergy's North Field East LNG expansion, capturing and storing ~2.1 Mtpa of CO₂. Under construction alongside the expansion.

properties.name: North Field South CCS
properties.description: A CCS project serving QatarEnergy's North Field South LNG expansion, capturing and storing ~1.2 Mtpa of CO₂. Under construction alongside the expansion.

properties.name: Ras Laffan CCS Expansion
properties.description: A major CCS project serving QatarEnergy's existing LNG facilities at Ras Laffan, with EPC awarded to Samsung C&T in November 2024. It will capture and sequester up to 4.1 Mtpa, among the world's largest CCS projects.

properties.name: Jubail CCS Hub
properties.location: Jubail Industrial City, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia
properties.description: Aramco, Linde and SLB are developing one of the world's largest CCS hubs, targeting ~9 Mtpa of CO₂ capture in its first phase by 2027 with expansion to ~14 Mtpa planned. CO₂ from Aramco gas plants and industrial sources will be stored in onshore saline aquifers.

properties.name: SACCCS Leandra Pilot
properties.operator: South African Centre for Carbon Capture & Storage (SACCCS)
properties.description: South Africa's pilot CO₂ storage project led by SACCCS, planned at Leandra in Mpumalanga. Long-delayed and still in early development as the country's first CO₂ injection pilot.

properties.name: BECCS Stockholm (Stockholm Exergi)
properties.description: World's first large-scale bioenergy with carbon capture and storage at a district-heating biomass plant, with FID taken in 2025 and biogenic CO₂ removal targeted by 2028.

properties.name: Heidelberg Materials Slite CCS
properties.description: Heidelberg Materials' planned carbon capture at the Slite cement plant on Gotland, Sweden's largest single industrial CO₂ emitter.

properties.name: Preem Lysekil CCS
properties.description: Planned carbon capture at Preem's Lysekil refinery to reduce refinery emissions.

properties.name: Bayu-Undan CCS
properties.description: Santos-led plan to convert the Bayu-Undan gas field, shared between Timor-Leste and Australia, into a large offshore CO₂ storage hub after gas production ends.

properties.name: Bab Gas Plant CCS
properties.description: A planned CO₂ capture project at ADNOC's Bab gas processing complex, with FEED awarded to Worley in late 2024. Part of ADNOC's target to reach 10 Mtpa of carbon capture capacity by 2030.

properties.name: Habshan CCS
properties.description: ADNOC Gas is building CO₂ capture units at the Habshan gas processing plant for permanent geological storage, with FID taken in September 2023. The project triples ADNOC's capture capacity to ~2.3 Mtpa.

properties.name: Acorn CCS
properties.description: Scottish CCS project capturing CO₂ at the St Fergus gas terminal for storage in the Goldeneye/Acorn offshore store; a UK Track-2 project led by Storegga with Shell and Harbour Energy.

properties.name: Drax BECCS
properties.description: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage at the Drax power station, aiming to remove millions of tonnes of CO₂ per year pending government support.

properties.name: EET Hydrogen (HPP1) Stanlow
properties.description: Blue hydrogen production at the Stanlow refinery with CO₂ capture routed to the HyNet cluster; the first plant (HPP1) is under construction.

properties.name: Encirc Elton CCS
properties.description: CO₂ capture at the Elton glass manufacturing site as part of the HyNet cluster.

properties.name: Eni Liverpool Bay CO₂ Storage
properties.location: Liverpool Bay, Irish Sea, United Kingdom
properties.description: Eni's offshore CO₂ storage hub in depleted Irish Sea gas fields, forming the storage arm of HyNet; FID taken October 2024.

properties.name: H2Teesside
properties.description: bp's planned large-scale blue hydrogen production facility at Teesside with CO₂ capture, feeding the East Coast Cluster.

properties.name: Hanson Padeswood CCS
properties.description: Carbon capture at Heidelberg Materials' Padeswood cement works, feeding the HyNet cluster.

properties.name: Medway / Isle of Grain Energy Hub
properties.location: Isle of Grain, Kent, United Kingdom
properties.description: National Grid Ventures' proposal to develop a CO₂ import and storage hub at the Isle of Grain LNG terminal.

properties.name: Morecambe Net Zero
properties.description: Spirit Energy's plan to store CO₂ in the depleted Morecambe Bay gas fields.

properties.name: Net Zero Teesside Industrial Capture
properties.description: Aggregates CO₂ capture from multiple Teesside industrial emitters, including CF Fertilisers, for transport to the Northern Endurance Partnership store.

properties.name: Net Zero Teesside Power (NZT Power)
properties.description: bp-Equinor gas-fired power station with integrated carbon capture at Teesside; FID taken in late 2024 with construction under way and operation expected around 2028.

properties.name: Northern Endurance Partnership
properties.location: Endurance saline aquifer, North Sea, United Kingdom
properties.description: Offshore CO₂ transport and storage system serving the East Coast Cluster, injecting into the Endurance saline aquifer; FID taken December 2024.

properties.name: Peak Cluster
properties.description: Planned capture network linking cement and lime plants in Derbyshire and Staffordshire to offshore storage.

properties.name: Solent Cluster
properties.description: ExxonMobil-led cluster at Fawley aiming to produce blue hydrogen and capture industrial CO₂ for offshore storage.

properties.name: Viking CCS
properties.description: Harbour Energy-led CO₂ transport and storage cluster in the Humber region, using the Viking depleted gas fields and targeting injection from around 2027.

properties.name: Viridor Runcorn CCS
properties.description: CO₂ capture at the Runcorn energy-from-waste plant, connecting to the HyNet cluster for transport and storage.

properties.name: ADM Cedar Rapids CCS
properties.description: Planned carbon capture and sequestration at ADM's Cedar Rapids ethanol complex, building on the company's Decatur, Illinois operations.

properties.name: Bayou Bend CCS
properties.description: Offshore CO₂ storage hub in Texas state waters of the Gulf of Mexico with large saline-storage capacity, positioned to serve Gulf Coast industrial emitters.

properties.name: Heirloom Carbon DAC (Louisiana)
properties.description: Direct air capture developer planning commercial limestone-based DAC capacity in Louisiana, tied to the Project Cypress hub and regional storage infrastructure.

properties.name: NET Power Project Permian
properties.description: First utility-scale NET Power oxy-combustion natural gas plant (~300 MW) designed to inherently capture its CO₂. Under construction in the Permian Basin with captured CO₂ targeted for enhanced oil recovery and storage.

properties.name: Project Bison
properties.description: Modular solid-sorbent direct air capture project planned in Wyoming with a long-term target of 5 Mtpa by 2030, supported by state incentives.

properties.name: Project Cypress DAC Hub
properties.description: DOE-supported regional direct air capture hub in southwest Louisiana combining multiple DAC technologies with dedicated saline storage. Awarded funding under the DOE Regional DAC Hubs program.

properties.name: Project Tundra
properties.description: Planned post-combustion CCS retrofit of the Milton R. Young lignite-fired power station, with CO₂ destined for enhanced oil recovery and saline storage in North Dakota.

properties.name: San Juan Generating Station CCS
properties.description: Proposed post-combustion CCS retrofit of the San Juan coal plant to capture most of its CO₂ for enhanced oil recovery in the Permian and San Juan basins. Facing financing and permitting hurdles.

properties.name: South Texas DAC Hub
properties.description: DOE-supported regional direct air capture hub on the King Ranch in south Texas, building on Stratos technology and targeting up to 1 Mtpa of removal with saline storage.

properties.name: Summit Carbon Solutions Pipeline
properties.description: Pipeline network designed to capture CO₂ from more than 50 ethanol plants across Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, South Dakota and North Dakota and transport it to permanent geologic storage in North Dakota. The largest planned US ethanol-carbon-capture system.

properties.name: Tallgrass Trailblazer CO2 Pipeline
properties.description: Proposed conversion of a natural gas pipeline into a CO₂ trunk line to move captured CO₂ from Wyoming and Nebraska emitters to geologic storage and enhanced oil recovery.

properties.name: Wabash Valley Resources
properties.description: Planned ammonia and fertilizer plant with CO₂ capture and injection into a deep saline formation in Indiana, a first-of-kind zero-emission ammonia facility in the state.
